rv.q: THE OFFICIAL BIOGRAPHY is a fascinating two-hander that brings a pair of completely different individuals together over the course of several months.
This is a smart play that asks big questions about the nature of truth.
As frustrating as this play is, there is much to like here—and above all, I am a critic who adores actors. You need to go watch The Official Biography because you need to go watch Gary Houston.
But a play about the slippery nature of truth needs to make us believe in the collaboration between the characters who are exploring it.
In the end, The Official Biography proves to be a compelling psychological duel—a fascinating game of cat and mouse.
Kurt McGinnis Brown has written a very compelling and engaging play that has the audience on the edge of their seats waiting to see what happens next.
For those that like to be slowly drawn in and keep guessing what is real and what is fiction, then The Official Biography would be a good fit for you!

The Official Biography shows a lot of promise, especially with its strong performances and thoughtful ideas. Still, the script would benefit from more development to create a clearer and more satisfying story for audiences.

cn.t: Strong performances anchor this two-hander exploring truth and fiction between opposing writers, but critics find the ambitious themes about authorship and power don't fully coalesce into a satisfying whole.
